lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 95: in split view, Insert drops the selected files on the other pane.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue ninety-five: in split view, Insert drops the selected files on the other pane.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You press Insert in split view, with files selected in the active pane.
The new window action checks split view, the selection, and the other pane's folder.
Then the drop rule, now in its own function, decides between move and copy.
The files move or copy into the other pane, and focus stays where it was.
The same action is in the Edit menu, greyed out without split view or a selection.
Drag and drop now calls the same rule, so its decisions don't change.
Before, moving files across split view took a drag, or Cut, a click and Paste; now one key does it.
Insert has no rule of its own: it shares the drop's move-or-copy code, so the two can't drift apart.
Shift+Insert and Ctrl+Insert were dropped from the issue, because they already paste and copy in Thunar.
lines.say: Shift Insert and Control Insert were dropped from the issue, because they already paste and copy in Thunar.

lines.caption: In a text field, such as the location bar, the field gets the key first, so Insert stays a text key.
With split view off or nothing selected, the key passes on; a folder that would refuse a drop gets nothing.
It moves when every file is on the same disk in a writable folder, or comes from the Trash; otherwise it copies.
The transfer uses Thunar's usual move or copy job, with progress and undo.
The menu item has no underlined letter, because every letter of its name is already taken in that menu.
Moving the rule out of the drag code also fixes a small memory leak.
Insert does nothing without split view, a selection, or a folder that would accept a drop, and leaves text fields alone.
Otherwise it moves on the same disk, copies across disks or from read-only folders, and moves into the Trash.
In the drag code, about 40 lines of loop became this one call to the new function.
lines.say: In the drag code, about forty lines of loop became this one call to the new function.

lines.caption: The PR changes four source files and adds its test, this page and its narration.
To undo it, revert this PR; it stores no setting.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It reuses the drop rule, the split-view code that finds the other pane, and the move and copy calls a drop makes.
In this session it built in the cloud container with no compiler warnings in the changed files.
The new test moved a file with Insert, left the location bar alone, and did nothing without split view.
The existing drag and drop test still passed, and all 12 tests passed.
lines.say: The existing drag and drop test still passed, and all twelve tests passed.

lines.caption: Not run: the copy case, which needs a read-only folder or a second disk, and moves into the Trash.
A fresh review agent read the diff and the issue twice: 7 findings, then 4 more, all low.
lines.say: A fresh review agent read the diff and the issue twice: seven findings, then four more, all low.

lines.caption: The high one: the two extra keys would have taken over Paste and Copy, which led to keeping only Insert.
Fixed: refuse read-only folders and Trash subfolders, skip files already there, and drop the clashing underlined letter.
Accepted: the side pane's focus, the menu item's state, and the untested copy and Trash cases.
CI's own review comes with the first push.
CI's run and screenshots come after the push; copying across disks waits for a real desktop.
The changes, CI's comments and the issue are linked here.
Part 3. Nothing depends on issue 95.
lines.say: Part 3. Nothing depends on issue ninety-five.

lines.caption: Always-copy and always-move keys could come back under other keys, in a new issue, if you want them.
In short: in split view, Insert now sends the selection to the other pane, just as a drop would.
